items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: But he and Scoville both played with the Rhythm Kings.

ctx.x: Well, I thought about that the Indiana school took liberties with rhythm, which I don't particularly remember the Chicago boys using. But they exchanged favors on such elements, did they?

Oh, yeah. The Wolverines were always waiting for Hoagie to come out with another crazy one, or the Marahue brothers down in Indiana. There were others around, you know, at that time. Bob Gillette, who played banjo with the Wolverines, played often with the Rhythm Kings. And Don Murray. And I think Don made angry with them. I think Don was with them a lot, as a matter of fact, on tenor, after Jack Pettis. When we were talking about taking up music as a profession on the part of the Austin boys, everybody knew that…
and so he was replaced with Don Murray in the band because of that
